DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)

I have reviewed your arterial blood gas results showing significant hypoxemia and respiratory acidosis, which is consistent with lung immaturity. Based on the clinical presentation of a newborn with respiratory distress and these specific blood gas findings, the most likely diagnosis is Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). This is a common condition in premature infants due to surfactant deficiency. I would like to confirm this with a chest X-ray to check for the classic "ground-glass" appearance and air bronchograms.
